info.title: Flashduty Open API
info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter created in the Flashduty console under My → APP Key (or sent in the `Fd-App-Key` header). Responses follow a uniform envelope: `{ request_id, data }` on success, `{ request_id, error }` on failure.

post.description: Batch invite new members to the organization by email or phone.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Members Manage** (`organization`) |

## Usage

- Each entry needs `email`, or `member_name` together with `phone`.
- Entries whose email or phone already belongs to a member of the account are skipped silently; `items` lists only the members created by this call and is `null` when none were created.
- New members are created in `pending` status and are sent an invitation by email or SMS.
- Emails are stored in lower case. If the account restricts member email domains, an address outside the allowlist returns `400`; duplicate emails or phones within one request also return `400`.
- `country_code` must be an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code (e.g. "CN"). It is validated and normalized to upper case before storage; invalid values are rejected with a 400.
- When a member's `phone` has no "+" prefix, it is parsed with that member's `country_code` as the region hint (defaults to "CN" when omitted).
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log. Don't put secrets in request fields.

post.description: Identify a member and reset the specified profile fields.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Identify the member with one of `member_id`, `member_name`, `email`, `phone`, or `ref_id`. If multiple identifiers are present, the server checks them in that order.
- The caller must be the account owner, the member themself, or hold the Admin role; otherwise the call returns `403 AccessDenied`.
- Put the fields to write under `updates`: `member_name`, `password`, `phone`, `country_code`, `email`, `avatar`, `locale`, `time_zone`, or `ref_id`. Omitted or `null` fields keep their current value; `updates` must carry at least one field.
- A new `member_name`, `email`, or `phone` must not belong to another member of the account; a conflict returns `400`. A changed `email` or `phone` is marked unverified unless `from` is `api` and the account has member invitations disabled.
- `updates.time_zone` set to an empty string clears the member's own time zone, so the member follows the account's.
- `updates.country_code` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code (e.g. "CN", "US"). It is an independently updatable field: `updates.phone` is not required, and the new region is stored even when the phone is unchanged. An explicit empty string is rejected with a 400.
- When `updates.phone` has no "+" prefix, it is parsed with `updates.country_code` as the region hint, falling back to the member's stored region and then to "CN". Legacy digit calling codes such as "86" remain accepted only as parsing hints — stored values are always ISO region codes.
- The top-level `country_code` is only a parsing hint for the identifying `phone`; it is never stored.
- Fields are written one at a time; if a later field fails validation, the fields written before it in the same call stay saved.
- Members provisioned through SSO cannot be changed while the SSO configuration marks them non-editable.
- Concurrent profile updates or invitations in the same account can return `429 RequestTooFrequently`; retry after a moment.
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log. Don't put secrets in request fields.

post.description: Return a cursor-paginated list of audit log entries within a time range.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Audit Read** (`organization`) |

## Usage

- Time range is required. Maximum span is 90 days. Both `start_time` and `end_time` are Unix epoch **seconds**.
- Use `search_after_ctx` from the previous response to fetch the next page. The token is opaque — do not construct it manually.
- The retention window depends on the account's license. Queries beyond the retention boundary silently return an empty result rather than an error.
- Pass an explicit `limit` (1–99) for predictable paging; when it is omitted or 0 the server chooses the page size, which may be the whole result set. Entries are returned newest first.

## Restrictions

| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |

post.description: Email account members a message written by the calling AI SRE session.

x-mint.content: ## Restrictions | Aspect | Value | | ------ | ----- | | Rate limits | **200 requests/minute**; **10 requests/second** per account | | Permissions | None — but see the credential requirement under Usage | ## Usage - Only callable with a credential minted for an AI SRE session; any other credential is rejected with `AccessDenied`. - Delivery is asynchronous — `accepted` means the email was queued, not that it was delivered. - Recipients that are not active members of the caller's account, or that have no email address on file, are skipped rather than failing the whole request. - Whether email is included follows each recipient's own notification preferences for this kind of message; a recipient with no preference set defaults to receiving it. - Recipients receive exactly the sanitized `html` as the email body, with nothing added around it. The sender name shows the caller's name followed by "(via AI SRE)". - Before sending, the server inspects the submitted `html` and rejects the request with `400` / `InvalidParameter` when it contains constructs whose removal would change what recipients see (`

400.description: The submitted `html` contains a construct that the sanitizer would otherwise remove and that would change what recipients see (see the `html` field description for the full list); the request is rejected instead, and nothing is queued.

error.message: email html contains 2 construct(s) the sanitizer removes, which would change what recipients see. Fix and send again:

AppKeyAuth.name: app_key
AppKeyAuth.description: APP Key created in the Flashduty console under My → APP Key. Send it as the `app_key` query parameter or in the `Fd-App-Key` request header. Its effective access is the intersection of the key's permission scope and the creator's current role permissions. Keep it secret.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request — usually a missing or malformed parameter.

error.message: The specified parameter is not valid.

Forbidden.description: The app_key is valid, but its permission scope or the creator's role does not allow this operation or object.

NotFound.description: The referenced resource does not exist or has been deleted. Note: Flashduty historically returns HTTP 400 with code `ResourceNotFound` for missing domain entities; a true 404 is reserved for unknown routes.

error.message: The resource you request is not found

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit hit (per-account limit or the operation's platform-wide limit). Wait for the number of seconds in `Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay`, then retry.

Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay.description: Seconds until the current rate-limit window resets. Absent when the request was rejected by the gateway's global protection limit.

ServerError.description: Unexpected server-side error. Include the request_id when reporting.

error.message: We encountered an internal error, and it has been reported. Please try again later.

created_at.description: Timestamp of the operation in Unix epoch milliseconds.

account_id.description: ID of the account the entry belongs to.

member_id.description: ID of the member who performed the action. 0 when the action was performed by the account principal itself.

member_name.description: Display name of the member. Empty when `member_id` is 0.

ip.description: Client IP address of the caller.

operation_name.description: Human-readable Chinese label of the operation (e.g. `创建模板`).

body.description: JSON-encoded request body. Bodies containing sensitive fields are base64url-encoded instead; bodies over 10 KB are replaced by a truncation placeholder.

Key.description: Name of a URL path parameter (the `:xxx` placeholder in the route).

Value.description: The actual value of that path parameter in this request.

params.description: URL path parameters as an array of `Key`/`Value` pairs (an empty array when none). Some deployments return the same array as a JSON-encoded string.

is_dangerous.description: True if this is flagged as a high-risk operation.

is_write.description: True for mutating operations; false for read-only ones.

principal_kind.description: Kind of the caller. `member` — a member or account-owner session; `service` — an app key or a short-lived key issued to AI SRE.

credential_type.description: Credential type used for the call. `app_key` for a long-lived console app key, `ephemeral_app_key` for a short-lived key issued to AI SRE, and an empty string for member sessions.

credential_id.description: ID of the credential (the app key ID) when `credential_type` is `app_key`; 0 otherwise.

items.description: Array of all auditable operation types (only APIs flagged for audit); always an array, possibly empty.

name.description: Stable machine-readable operation name for use as a filter.

name_cn.description: Human-readable Chinese label shown in the console.

AuditSearchRequest.description: Filter criteria for audit log search. Time range is required.

start_time.description: Start of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Exclusive — entries at exactly this second are not included.

end_time.description: End of the search window, Unix epoch seconds. Inclusive. Must be after `start_time`; maximum span 90 days.

limit.description: Page size, 0–99. Omit or set to 0 to let the server choose the page size (it may return every matching entry).

request_id.description: Filter to a single request by its unique request ID.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous response. Leave empty for the first page.

operations.description: Filter to specific operation names. Use `POST /audit/operation/list` to get the valid set.

person_id.description: Filter by the operator's member ID (get IDs from `POST /member/list`). Pass the account ID to match actions performed by the account principal itself.

is_dangerous.description: When true, return only high-risk (dangerous) operations.

is_write.description: When true, return only write operations; when false, return only read operations.

total.description: Total matching entries in the search window.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty string when there are no more results.

docs.description: Audit log entries for this page, newest first. Omitted when the page is empty.

DutyError.description: Error payload inside the response envelope. Present only on non-2xx responses.

message.description: Human-readable error message in the response language (`locale` / `lang` query parameter or `Accept-Language` header). May name the offending field; do not parse it.
message.example: The specified parameter template_id is not valid.

ErrorCode.description:
Error code. Every failed response sets `error.code` to one of these stable strings; branch on it rather than on the HTTP status.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OK` | 200 | Reserved; never returned on a failed request. |
| `InvalidParameter` | 400 | A parameter is missing, has the wrong type, or failed validation; `message` usually names the field. |
| `BadRequest` | 400 | The request breaks a business rule or conflicts with the current state of an object; `message` says which. |
| `InvalidContentType` | 400 | The body is not sent as `application/json`. |
| `ResourceNotFound` | 400 | The referenced object does not exist in this account or was deleted. Returned as HTTP 400, not 404. |
| `NoLicense` | 400 | The account's plan does not include the feature, a plan quota is used up, the plan has expired, or credits are insufficient. |
| `ReferenceExist` | 400 | The object is still referenced by other objects, so it cannot be deleted. |
| `Unauthorized` | 401 | The APP Key is missing, invalid, or deleted. |
| `BalanceNotEnough` | 402 | Console-only (billing); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `AccessDenied` | 403 | The APP Key's permission scope or the creator's role does not allow this operation or object. |
| `RouteNotFound` | 404 | No operation matches the HTTP method and path. |
| `MethodNotAllowed` | 405 | The path exists but not for this HTTP method. |
| `UndonedOrderExist` | 409 | Console-only (billing); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `EntityTooLarge` | 413 | The request body exceeds the size limit. |
| `RequestLocked` | 423 | Console-only (sign-in protection); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `RequestVerifyRequired` | 428 | Console-only (verification code); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `DangerousOperation` | 428 | Console-only (MFA for high-risk actions); not returned by Open API operations. |
| `RequestTooFrequently` | 429 | A rate limit was hit; wait for the `Flashcat-Request-Rate-Limit-Delay` response header (seconds) before retrying. |
| `InternalError` | 500 | Unexpected server error; retry with backoff and include `request_id` when reporting. |
| `ServiceUnavailable` | 503 | A backend dependency is overloaded or unavailable; retry with backoff. |

ErrorResponse.description: Response envelope for errors. `error` is required; `data` is absent.

request_id.description: Unique trace ID of this request; include it when reporting issues so logs can be located.

InviteMemberItem.description: A member to invite. Identify the invitee by `email` alone, or by `member_name` + `phone` together.

member_name.description: Display name, 2–39 characters. Required when `email` is not provided; derived from the email prefix when omitted.

email.description: Email address, stored in lower case. Required when `phone` is not provided.

phone.description: Phone number. Required when `email` is not provided.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code for `phone` (e.g. "CN"). Validated and normalized to upper case before storage; invalid values are rejected with a 400. Also the parsing hint when `phone` has no "+" prefix (defaults to "CN").

role_ids.description: Role IDs to assign: built-in `2` (Admin), `6` (Responder), `8` (Viewer), or custom role IDs from `POST /role/list`. Defaults to Viewer (`8`) when omitted; an ID that does not exist returns `400`.

locale.description: Locale: `zh-CN` (Simplified Chinese) or `en-US` (English); other values are rejected with a 400. Defaults to the account's locale when omitted.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone name such as `Asia/Shanghai`. Omit it to have the member follow the account's time zone; an invalid name returns `400`.

ref_id.description: External reference ID (for example an employee ID in an HR system), usable later as a lookup key in `POST /member/delete` and `POST /member/info/reset`.

MemberDeleteRequest.description: Delete member request (provide one of the lookup fields)

member_id.description: Member ID. When several lookup fields are provided, the first non-empty one wins in the order `member_id` > `member_name` > `email` > `phone` > `ref_id`

member_name.description: Member name. Only used when `member_id` is not provided

email.description: Email address. Only used when neither `member_id` nor `member_name` is provided

phone.description: Phone number. Only used when `member_id`, `member_name`, and `email` are all absent

country_code.description: Region hint for parsing `phone` when it has no "+" prefix — an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "CN" (the default when omitted). Legacy digit calling codes like "86" are still accepted in this parsing context.

ref_id.description: External reference ID. Only used when all other lookup fields are absent

is_force.description: Skip the reference check. When false (default), the call fails with `ReferenceExist` if the member belongs to a team, is targeted by an escalation rule, or is in a schedule. A forced delete does not remove those references.

account_id.description: ID of the account the member belongs to.

account_email.description: Contact email of the account owner.

account_role_ids.description: IDs of the roles assigned to the member; resolve them with `POST /role/list`.

account_locale.description: Account-level locale preference (e.g. zh-CN or en-US). Omitted when the account has none set.

account_time_zone.description: The account's IANA time zone setting; empty string when the account has none. Always present.

resolved_time_zone.description: Effective time zone to render times in: the member's `time_zone` if valid, otherwise the account's, otherwise `Asia/Shanghai`. Always present.

domain.description: Account domain, the subdomain used to sign in to the console.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code of the member's contact phone (e.g. "CN", "US", "HK").

locale.description: Member's locale preference. Omitted when the member has none set.

time_zone.description: The member's own IANA time zone setting; empty string when the member follows the account's time zone. Always present.

created_at.description: Member creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

mp_plat.description: Cloud marketplace the account was provisioned from: `aws` — AWS Marketplace. Omitted when the account did not come from a marketplace.

mp_account_id.description: Account identifier on the marketplace platform. Omitted together with `mp_plat`.

members.description: Members to invite in one call (at least 1). Each entry needs either an `email`, or `member_name` + `phone` together.

from.description: Invite source. Only takes effect when the account has member invites disabled and the value is `api`: members are created directly in the enabled state with email/phone marked verified and no invitation sent. Any other value follows the normal invite flow

items.description: Members created by this call; entries skipped because they already exist are not listed. `null` when no member was created.

account_id.description: ID of the account the member belongs to.

member_id.description: Member ID; the same value is used as the person ID in other APIs (for example `person_ids`).

member_name.description: Display name, unique in the account.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code of the member's contact phone (e.g. "CN", "US", "HK").

phone.description: Phone number in E.164 form with the middle digits masked (for example `+86151****6519`); empty string when unset.

email.description: Email address in lower case; empty string when unset.

locale.description: Locale preference. Not populated by `POST /member/list`, so it is always omitted there.

time_zone.description: The member's own IANA time zone setting (for example `Asia/Shanghai`). Omitted when unset, which means the member follows the account's time zone; `POST /member/info` returns the effective zone.

phone_verified.description: `true` once the member has verified the phone number.

email_verified.description: `true` once the member has verified the email address.

avatar.description: Avatar image URL or path; empty string when unset.

status.description: Member status. `enabled` — active member; `pending` — invited but has not accepted yet. Removed members are not listed.

account_role_ids.description: IDs of the roles assigned to the member: built-in `2` (Admin), `6` (Responder), `8` (Viewer), or custom role IDs from `POST /role/list`.

is_external.description: `true` when the member was provisioned through SSO rather than invited or registered.

ref_id.description: External reference ID (for example an employee ID in an HR system); empty string when unset.

role_id.description: Filter by role ID. Get role IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer)

member_id.description: Filter by member ID. Return only the member with this ID.

p.description: Page number, starting at 1. Defaults to the first page.

limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 100 on the server when omitted or 0

query.description: Keyword. Matches a substring of the member name or email; a numeric keyword also matches an exact member ID, and a keyword that parses as a phone number (without `+`, parsed as a Chinese number) also matches the exact phone.

p.description: Page number from the request; `0` when `p` was omitted (the first page is returned).

limit.description: Page size applied; 100 when `limit` was omitted.

total.description: Number of members matching the filters, across all pages.

items.description: Members on this page; empty array when none match.

MemberResetInfoRequest.description: Reset member info request. Top-level fields identify the member, and updates contains the profile fields to write.

member_id.description: Member ID used to identify the member.

member_name.description: Member name used to identify the member.

email.description: Email address used to identify the member.

phone.description: Phone number used to identify the member. Include country_code when the number is not in E.164 format.

country_code.description: Region hint for parsing `phone` when it has no "+" prefix — an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as "CN" (the default when omitted). Legacy digit calling codes like "86" are still accepted in this parsing context.

ref_id.description: External reference ID used to identify the member.

from.description: Set to `api` to mark an updated phone or email as verified. Only takes effect when the account has member invites disabled; any other value is ignored.

updates.description: New profile values to write. Must include at least one field.

MemberResetInfoUpdates.description: Member profile fields to write. Omitted fields remain unchanged.

member_name.description: New display name, 2–39 characters, unique in the account.

password.description: New login password in the encrypted format accepted by the backend.

phone.description: New phone number; include `country_code` when it is not in E.164 format. Must not belong to another member; the new number is marked unverified (see `from`).

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code (e.g. "CN", "US"). Updated independently — `phone` is not required — and also used as the parsing hint for `phone`. Invalid values are rejected with a 400; an explicit empty string is not allowed.

email.description: New email address. Must not belong to another member; the new address is marked unverified (see `from`).

locale.description: New locale preference. One of: `zh-CN` (Simplified Chinese), `en-US` (English); other values are rejected with a 400.

time_zone.description: New IANA time zone name such as `Asia/Shanghai`; an empty string clears it so the member follows the account's time zone. An invalid name returns `400`.

ref_id.description: New external reference ID; an empty string clears it.

member_id.description: ID of the member whose roles change (from `POST /member/list`).

role_ids.description: Role IDs to grant; appended to the member's current roles (duplicates are deduplicated).

member_id.description: ID of the member whose roles change (from `POST /member/list`).

role_ids.description: Role IDs to remove from the member.

member_id.description: ID of the member whose roles change (from `POST /member/list`).

role_ids.description: New role ID set; replaces the member's existing roles entirely (not additive). Get IDs from `POST /role/list`.

member_id.description: ID of the newly created member.

member_name.description: Display name stored for the member; derived from the email prefix when `member_name` was omitted.

factor_type.description: Factor type. `api`: backend API factor — `factor_name` is the API name (e.g. `skill:write:upload`), enforced at the gateway; `button`: UI action factor, used by the role-config page to render action toggles; `visit`: page-visit factor (custom menu pages use this type); `menu`: menu-visibility factor (legacy, no current seed data); `url`: page route-path factor (legacy, no current seed data).

source.description: Origin of the factor. `system` — seeded built-in factor; `account` — dynamic factor created for this account (e.g. custom menus).

source_ref.description: Primary key of the source object (e.g. the custom menu ID) for account-scoped factors. Omitted when empty.

permission_type.description: Whether this is a read or manage permission. `read`: view-only permission (read/list/query); `manage`: administrative permission covering mutations (create, update, delete, configure).

scope.description:
Functional scope the permission applies to.

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `account` | Account settings and API keys |
| `organization` | Members, teams, roles, audit |
| `on-call` | On-call incident management |
| `monit` | Monitoring |
| `rum` | Real user monitoring |
| `ai-sre` | AI SRE features |
| `custom_menu` | Account-defined custom menu pages (on-premises only) |

status.description: Permission status. `enabled` — active; `deleted` — removed (deleted permissions are filtered out and never returned).

is_granted.description: Whether this permission is granted to the roles given in `role_ids`. Always present in this endpoint's response; `false` entries only appear when `with_all` is true.

account_id.description: Owning account ID. Omitted when 0, i.e. for system-level permissions.

source.description: Origin of the permission. `system` — seeded built-in permission; `account` — dynamic permission created for this account (e.g. custom menus).

source_ref.description: Primary key of the source object (e.g. the custom menu ID) for account-scoped permissions. Omitted when empty.

PersonInfosRequest.description: Get person info by IDs request

person_ids.description: Person IDs to look up — these are member IDs (get them from `POST /member/list`). Passing the account ID returns the account principal; unknown IDs are ignored

account_id.description: ID of the account the person belongs to.

person_id.description: Person ID: the account ID for the account owner, otherwise the member ID.

locale.description: Locale preference (`zh-CN` or `en-US`). Omitted when unset.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone setting: the member's own setting, or the account's for the account owner. Omitted when unset (a member without a setting follows the account's time zone).

phone.description: Phone number. Omitted when empty — this endpoint never populates it.

phone_verified.description: Whether the phone is verified. Always false in this endpoint's response.

email_verified.description: `true` when the email address is verified; for the account owner, `true` whenever an email is set.

as.description: Principal kind: `account` — the account owner principal; `member` — an organization member.

status.description: Person status. `enabled` — active; `pending` — invited but not yet accepted; `deleted` — removed. Omitted when empty.

PlatformEmptyObject.description: Empty object returned on success for operations with no meaningful payload.

RoleGrantRequest.description: Request to grant or revoke a role from members.

member_ids.description: IDs of the members to grant the role to or revoke it from (from `POST /member/list`). All must be members of the account; duplicates are rejected.

role_id.description: Role ID to grant or revoke. Get IDs from `POST /role/list`.
Role ID to operate on. Get IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer).
Role ID to query. Get IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer).

RoleItem.description: A role and its permission set.

role_id.description: Role ID. Built-in roles use the fixed IDs `2` (Admin), `6` (Responder), and `8` (Viewer).

role_name.description: Role name, unique in the account. The built-in roles are named `Admin`, `Responder`, and `Viewer` in every language.

description.description: Role description. For built-in roles it is localized by the request language.

status.description: Role status. `enabled` — active; `disabled` — turned off with `POST /role/disable`. Built-in roles are always `enabled`; deleted roles are never returned.

permission_ids.description: IDs of the permissions the role grants, in ascending order; resolve them with `POST /role/permission/list`. Empty array when none.

editable.description: `false` for the built-in roles (Admin, Responder, Viewer); `true` for custom roles.

created_at.description: Time the role was created, Unix timestamp in seconds. Built-in roles carry a fixed timestamp.

updated_at.description: Unix epoch seconds the role was last updated.

no_global.description: When true, exclude the built-in global roles (Admin, Responder, Viewer) and return only custom roles. Default: false.

total.description: Number of roles returned: custom roles plus the 3 built-in roles unless `no_global` is true.

items.description: Array of roles; includes account roles plus built-in global roles unless `no_global=true`; empty array when no results.

role_ids.description: Role IDs (built-in or custom) whose granted permissions to return or mark. IDs that do not exist are ignored.

with_all.description: When true, return every permission and use `is_granted` to mark the ones granted by `role_ids`. When false (default), return only the granted permissions.

items.description: Array of permission items: system-level permissions plus the caller's account-scoped custom-menu permissions (never other tenants' rows).

RoleUpsertRequest.description: Parameters for creating or updating a custom role.

role_id.description: ID of the custom role to update. Omit or set to 0 to create a new role. Do not pass the built-in role IDs `2`, `6`, or `8`.

description.description: Role description, up to 499 characters. Omitting it on update clears the stored description.

permission_ids.description: IDs of the permissions the role grants (from `POST /role/permission/list`). Replaces the existing set; omitting it or sending an empty array leaves the role with no permissions.

role_name.description: Role name echoed from the request.

SuccessEnvelope.description: Success response envelope. On every 2xx response, `request_id` identifies the call (also mirrored in the `Flashcat-Request-Id` header) and `data` holds the endpoint-specific payload. Failure responses use a different shape — see `ErrorResponse`.

request_id.description: Unique ID for this request. Mirrored in the Flashcat-Request-Id response header. Include it when reporting issues.

data.description: Operation-specific payload, documented in each operation's 200 response. Operations without a payload return `{}` or omit `data` entirely.

TeamBriefItem.description: Brief team info for batch responses.

team_id.description: Team ID, one of the requested `team_ids`.

team_name.description: Team name. Deleted teams are included, so this can be the name of a team that no longer appears in `POST /team/list`.

person_ids.description: Array of person IDs belonging to the team; empty array (never null) when the team has no members.

TeamDeleteRequest.description: Request identifying a team to delete.

team_id.description: Team ID. At least one of the three lookup fields is required; when several are provided, `team_id` wins.

team_name.description: Team name. Only used when `team_id` is not provided.

ref_id.description: External reference ID. Only used when neither `team_id` nor `team_name` is provided.

TeamInfoRequest.description: Request identifying a team by one of ID, name, or external ref.

team_id.description: Team ID. At least one of the three lookup fields is required; lowest priority — only used when neither `ref_id` nor `team_name` is provided.

team_name.description: Team name. Only used when `ref_id` is not provided; takes precedence over `team_id`.

ref_id.description: External reference ID. When provided, takes precedence over `team_name` and `team_id`.

TeamInfosRequest.description: Request for batch team lookup by IDs.

team_ids.description: List of team IDs to look up.

items.description: Brief info for the matched teams, including deleted ones; `null` when no ID matches.

team_name.description: Team display name. 1–39 characters, unique per account.

status.description: Team status. `enabled` — active; `deleted` — soft-deleted (only possible when fetching a deleted team by `team_id`; list and name/ref_id lookups exclude deleted teams).

updated_by_name.description: Name of the last editor: the member's name, or the account name when the account owner made the change; empty string when unknown.

updated_by.description: Member ID of the last editor.

creator_name.description: Display name of the creator. Not populated by current endpoints — always an empty string; resolve `creator_id` via `POST /person/infos`.

created_at.description: Unix epoch seconds the team was created.

updated_at.description: Unix epoch seconds the team was last updated.

person_ids.description: Person IDs of the team's members (member IDs; the account owner's ID when the owner is in the team). Empty array when the team has no members.

ref_id.description: External reference ID for third-party HR system integration.

person_id.description: Filter by member ID — return only teams this person belongs to.

query.description: Substring match on team name or description.

p.description: Page number from the request; `0` when `p` was omitted (the first page is returned).

limit.description: Page size applied; 20 when `limit` was omitted.

total.description: Number of non-deleted teams matching the filters, across all pages.

items.description: Array of teams for the current page, used with `p`, `limit` and `total` for pagination; empty array on an empty page.

TeamUpsertRequest.description: Parameters for creating or updating a team.

team_id.description: ID of the team to update. Omit or set to 0 to create a new team; a non-zero ID must belong to an existing team of the account.

description.description: Free-form description, up to 500 characters. On update, omitting it clears the stored description.

person_ids.description: Person IDs to place in the team (member IDs, or the account ID for the account owner). Together with `emails` and `phones` they replace the entire member list; IDs that are not members of the account are ignored.

emails.description: Emails of existing members to place in the team; merged with `person_ids` and `phones`. Addresses that match no member are ignored and no invitation is sent.

phones.description: Phone numbers of existing members to place in the team; merged with `person_ids` and `emails`. Numbers without a `+` prefix are parsed with `countryCode`; an unparseable number fails the whole request with `400`, and numbers that match no member are ignored.

countryCode.description: Region hint for `phones` entries without a `+` prefix: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code such as `CN` (the default when omitted) or a digit calling code such as `86`.

ref_id.description: External reference ID (for example a department ID in an HR system), usable as a lookup key in `POST /team/info` and `POST /team/delete`. On update, omitting it clears the stored value.

reset_if_name_exist.description: When true and `team_id` is 0, an existing team with the same `team_name` is updated in place instead of returning a name-conflict error.

team_name.description: Team name echoed from the request.

account_name.description: Account (organization) name shown in the console.

phone.description: Account contact phone, masked for privacy.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 region code of the contact phone (e.g. "CN", "US", "HK").

locale.description: Account language preference (`zh-CN` or `en-US`); empty string when not set.

time_zone.description: Account default time zone (IANA name, e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`); members without their own setting follow it. Empty string when not set.

created_at.description: Account creation time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

restrictions.description: Account access restrictions. Omitted when none are configured.

ips.description: Source IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to call the console and API for this account; `null` or empty when unrestricted.

email_domains.description: Email domains allowed for new members; invitations to other domains are rejected. `null` or empty when unrestricted.

allow_subdomain.description: Whether subdomains of the allowed email domains are also accepted.

mp_plat.description: Cloud marketplace the account was provisioned from: `aws` — AWS Marketplace. Omitted when the account did not come from a marketplace.

mp_account_id.description: Account identifier on the marketplace platform. Omitted together with `mp_plat`.

role_id.description: Role ID to delete. Get IDs from `POST /role/list` (built-in roles: 2=Admin, 6=Responder, 8=Viewer).

is_force.description: When false (default), deletion fails with `ReferenceExist` while members still hold the role, listing them in `data.refs`. When true, the role is first revoked from all holders and then deleted. Does not bypass the SSO default-role check.

person_ids.description: Recipient member IDs. Optional, up to 20, no duplicates. Omitted or empty sends to the caller only.

subject.description: Email subject, used as written. Required, 1–200 characters. Line breaks are replaced with a space; leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed.

html.description: Email body as an HTML fragment (no ``/``/`` wrapper needed); recipients receive it as the whole email body. Required, up to 102,400 bytes of raw UTF-8 input (larger messages are clipped by common email clients), and must be non-empty after sanitization. `

recipients.description: One result per resolved recipient, in the same order as the resolved recipient list.

agent_instructions.description: Present when the submitted HTML body does not follow the default email layout (no `max-width:600px` wrapper table): guidance telling the calling AI SRE agent how to conform. Advisory only — a format the caller deliberately chose needs no change.

status.description: Delivery status. `accepted` — the email was queued for asynchronous delivery; `skipped` — no email was queued, see `reason`.

reason.description: Why the recipient was skipped. Only present when `status` is `skipped`. `not_member` — not an active member of the caller's account; `no_email` — the member has no email address on file; `email_disabled` — the member's notification preferences for this kind of message exclude email; `duplicate` — this recipient already received a message from the same AI SRE session turn; `rate_limited` — this recipient has already been sent 20 emails through this endpoint within the last hour; `send_failed` — enqueueing the email failed.
